candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration and client education
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — oral electrolyte replacement
candidate.educational_objective: Teach safe oral administration of potassium chloride extended-release tablets to reduce gastrointestinal irritation.

options.A: Take the tablets on an empty stomach to maximize absorption
options.B: Take the tablets with meals and with a glass of water or other liquid
options.C: Take the medication only once each week regardless of the prescribed dose
options.D: Chew the extended-release tablets thoroughly before swallowing

candidate.rationale: Current DailyMed labeling instructs that potassium chloride extended-release tablets be taken with meals and with a glass of water or other liquid and not on an empty stomach because of gastric irritation risk. Product-specific instructions should be followed for swallowing or alternative administration. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Potassium chloride extended-release tablets should be taken with meals and liquid and should not be taken on an empty stomach because of potential gastric irritation.
candidate.source_locator: Dosage and Administration — take with meals and with a glass of water or other liquid; do not take on an empty stomach
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine (official FDA drug labeling)
candidate.stem: A client is prescribed potassium chloride extended-release tablets. Which instruction should the nurse include?
